[0] Earlier rumours suggested Apple was preparing a 20th anniversary edition iPhone for next year, featuring an all-glass new design. However, analysts at investment bank Jefferies believe that device is no longer being pushed forward.

[1] Wall Street analyst says the bold redesign plan for the 20th anniversary iPhone has been cancelled.

[2] Wall Street investment bank Jefferies today downgraded Apple's stock rating to "Underperform," with analyst Edison Lee noting that the possible cancellation of the 20th anniversary iPhone redesign is one of the main reasons for the downgrade.

[3] The key to this downgrade lies in the alleged cancellation of Apple's all-glass iPhone. Although rumours of the project in development surfaced as early as 2025, with some suggesting it could launch as early as 2027, Apple has never responded to the speculation. However, the company quietly filed a patent for a "six-sided glass enclosure" back in 2019. Jefferies had previously considered the launch of an all-glass iPhone to be reasonable and credible, but Lee believes development work has stalled. The analyst noted that supply chain checks indicate the project was killed off due to poor yield rates. Lee believes that with memory costs soaring, this decision deals a "major blow" to driving sales of premium iPhones. If the device launched as planned in September 2027 to celebrate the iPhone's 20th anniversary, he estimates the blended retail price would reach US$2,060, higher than the average selling price of any previous model. Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe Apple originally planned to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further raising average selling prices and profits." He believes that with memory prices rising, this move was supposed to be a crucial defensive strategy.

[4] Lee also pointed out that Apple's artificial intelligence strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are further reasons for the downgrade of the company's stock rating.

[5] From Lee's report, it is unclear whether the analyst believes the entire redesign has been shelved, or only certain design elements have been scrapped.

[6] The most-liked comment was posted by Currentinterest

[7] These analysts have been wrong too many times when it comes to predictions about Apple's future plans. Even the term "all glass" may have never accurately captured what Apple truly intends to do. The 20th anniversary phone will be uniquely innovative and have no trouble selling, regardless of the final design.

[8] For example, there has long been speculation that Apple will not be able to completely remove the "Dynamic Island" cutout next year. Therefore, an "all glass" screen will be impossible to achieve. However, the rumoured four-curved-edge design may still launch.

[9] In any case, if the iPhone 20th anniversary edition design has indeed been cancelled, credible media outlets will likely confirm it soon.
